33: // CommitHook is an abstraction for executing arbitrary commands after atomic database commits
34: type CommitHook interface {
35: 	// Execute is arbitrary read-only function whose arguments are new Dataset commit into a specific Database.
36: 	// The returned values are a callback function and an error. The callback function is
37: 	// a Wait function which is optional. If returned, it will be registered with the ReplicationStatusController. If the
38: 	// hook implements NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook, it will be notified if the Wait function returns an error.
39: 	// The |Error| returned is actually ignored by the caller. It exists primarily for for unit testing. Any error which
40: 	// happens in a hook should be logged by the hook itself.
41: 	Execute(ctx context.Context, ds datas.Dataset, db *DoltDB) (func(context.Context) error, error)
42: 	// ExecuteForWorkingSets returns whether or not the hook should be executed for working set updates
43: 	ExecuteForWorkingSets() bool
44: 	// ExecuteForReplicaWrite returns whether or not the hook should be executed
45: 	// for writes received through the remotesapi endpoint as a cluster standby
46: 	// replica. Hooks like auto GC and stats should return true, while replication
47: 	// hooks (cluster replication, push-on-write) should return false to avoid
48: 	// replication loops.
49: 	ExecuteForReplicaWrite() bool
50: }
51: 
52: // NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook is an optional interface that can be implemented by CommitHooks.
53: // If a commit hook supports this interface, it can be notified if waiting for
54: // replication in the callback returned by |Execute| failed to complete in time
55: // or returned an error.
56: type NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook interface {
57: 	NotifyWaitFailed()
58: }
59: 
60: func (db hooksDatabase) SetCommitHooks(ctx context.Context, postHooks []CommitHook) hooksDatabase {
61: 	db.hooks = make([]CommitHook, len(postHooks))
62: 	copy(db.hooks, postHooks)
63: 	return db
64: }
65: 
66: func (db hooksDatabase) withReplicationStatusController(rsc *ReplicationStatusController) hooksDatabase {
67: 	db.rsc = rsc
68: 	return db
69: }
70: 
71: func (db hooksDatabase) PostCommitHooks() []CommitHook {
72: 	toret := make([]CommitHook, len(db.hooks))
73: 	copy(toret, db.hooks)
74: 	return toret
75: }
76: 
77: func (db hooksDatabase) ExecuteCommitHooks(ctx context.Context, ds datas.Dataset, onlyWS bool, replicaWrite bool) {
78: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
79: 	rsc := db.rsc
80: 	var ioff int
81: 	if rsc != nil {
82: 		ioff = len(rsc.Wait)
83: 		rsc.Wait = append(rsc.Wait, make([]func(context.Context) error, len(db.hooks))...)
84: 		rsc.NotifyWaitFailed = append(rsc.NotifyWaitFailed, make([]func(), len(db.hooks))...)
85: 	}
86: 	for il, hook := range db.hooks {
87: 		if (!onlyWS || hook.ExecuteForWorkingSets()) && (!replicaWrite || hook.ExecuteForReplicaWrite()) {
88: 			i := il
89: 			hook := hook
90: 			wg.Add(1)
91: 			go func() {
92: 				defer wg.Done()
93: 				// The error returned is intentionally ignored here. Hooks are expected to log errors themselves. The interface returns
94: 				// the error primarily for testing purposes.
95: 				f, _ := hook.Execute(ctx, ds, db.db)
96: 				if rsc != nil {
97: 					rsc.Wait[i+ioff] = f
98: 					if nf, ok := hook.(NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook); ok {
99: 						rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i+ioff] = nf.NotifyWaitFailed
100: 					} else {
101: 						rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i+ioff] = func() {}
102: 					}
103: 				}
104: 			}()
105: 		}
106: 	}
107: 	wg.Wait()
108: 	if rsc != nil {
109: 		j := ioff
110: 		for i := ioff; i < len(rsc.Wait); i++ {
111: 			// compact out any nil entries
112: 			if rsc.Wait[i] != nil {
113: 				rsc.Wait[j] = rsc.Wait[i]
114: 				rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[j] = rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i]
115: 				j++
116: 			}
117: 		}
118: 		rsc.Wait = rsc.Wait[:j]
119: 		rsc.NotifyWaitFailed = rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[:j]
120: 	}
121: }

42: // Database provides versioned storage for noms values. While Values can be
43: // directly read and written from a Database, it is generally more appropriate
44: // to read data by inspecting the Head of a Dataset and write new data by
45: // updating the Head of a Dataset via Commit() or similar. Particularly, new
46: // data is not guaranteed to be persistent until after a Commit (Delete,
47: // SetHeadToCommit, or FastForward) operation completes.
48: // The Database API is stateful, meaning that calls to GetDataset() or
49: // Datasets() occurring after a call to Commit() (et al) will represent the
50: // result of the Commit().
51: type Database interface {
52: 	// Close must have no side-effects
53: 	io.Closer
54: 
55: 	// Datasets returns the root of the database which is a
56: 	// Map<String, Ref<Commit>> where string is a datasetID.
57: 	Datasets(ctx context.Context) (DatasetsMap, error)
58: 
59: 	// GetDataset returns a Dataset struct containing the current mapping of
60: 	// datasetID in the above Datasets Map.
61: 	GetDataset(ctx context.Context, datasetID string) (Dataset, error)
62: 
63: 	// DatasetsByRootHash returns all datasets as of the root hash given
64: 	DatasetsByRootHash(ctx context.Context, rootHash hash.Hash) (DatasetsMap, error)
65: 
66: 	// GetDatasetByRootHash returns a Dataset struct containing the mapping of datasetId in the Datasets map as it
67: 	// existed at the root hash given.
68: 	GetDatasetByRootHash(ctx context.Context, datasetID string, rootHash hash.Hash) (Dataset, error)
69: 
70: 	// BuildNewCommit creates a new Commit struct for the provided dataset,
71: 	// but does not modify the dataset. This allows the commit to be inspected
72: 	// if necessary before any update is performed.
73: 	BuildNewCommit(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, v types.Value, opts CommitOptions) (*Commit, error)
74: 
75: 	// Commit updates the Commit that ds.ID() in this database points at. All
76: 	// Values that have been written to this Database are guaranteed to be
77: 	// persistent after Commit() returns successfully.
78: 	//
79: 	// The new Commit struct is constructed using v, opts.ParentsList, and
80: 	// opts.Meta. If opts.ParentsList is empty then the head value from
81: 	// |ds| is used as the parent. If opts.Meta is the zero value the
82: 	// Commit struct as an empty Meta struct.
83: 	//
84: 	// If the update cannot be performed because the existing dataset head
85: 	// is not a common ancestor of the constructed commit struct, returns
86: 	// an 'ErrMergeNeeded' error.
87: 	Commit(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, v types.Value, opts CommitOptions) (Dataset, error)
88: 
89: 	// WriteCommit has the same behavior as Commit but accepts an already-constructed Commit
90: 	// instead of constructing one from a Value and CommitOptions
91: 	WriteCommit(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, commit *Commit) (Dataset, error)
92: 
93: 	// Tag stores an immutable reference to a Commit. It takes a Hash to
94: 	// the Commit and a Dataset whose head must be nil (ie a newly created
95: 	// Dataset).  The new Tag struct is constructed pointing at
96: 	// |commitAddr| and metadata about the tag contained in the struct
97: 	// `opts.Meta`.
98: 	Tag(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, commitAddr hash.Hash, opts TagOptions) (Dataset, error)
99: 
100: 	// SetTuple puts an arbitrary byte array into the chunkstore.
101: 	// The dataset reference keys access to the value.
102: 	SetTuple(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, val []byte) (Dataset, error)
103: 
104: 	// UpdateStashList updates the stash list dataset only with given address hash to the updated stash list.
105: 	// The new/updated stash list address should be obtained before calling this function depending on
106: 	// whether add or remove a stash actions have been performed. This function does not perform any actions
107: 	// on the stash list itself.
108: 	UpdateStashList(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, stashListAddr hash.Hash) (Dataset, error)
109: 
110: 	// SetStatsRef updates the singleton statisics ref for this database.
111: 	SetStatsRef(context.Context, Dataset, hash.Hash) (Dataset, error)
112: 
113: 	// UpdateWorkingSet updates the dataset given, setting its value to a new
114: 	// working set value object with the ref and meta given. If the dataset given
115: 	// already had a value, it must match the hash given or this method returns
116: 	// ErrOptimisticLockFailed and the caller must retry.
117: 	// The returned Dataset is always the newest snapshot, regardless of
118: 	// success or failure, and Datasets() is updated to match backing storage
119: 	// upon return as well.
120: 	UpdateWorkingSet(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, workingSet WorkingSetSpec, prevHash hash.Hash) (Dataset, error)
121: 
122: 	// CommitWithWorkingSet combines Commit and UpdateWorkingSet, combining the parameters of both. It uses the
123: 	// pessimistic lock that UpdateWorkingSet does, asserting that the hash |prevWsHash| given is still the current one
124: 	// before attempting to write a new value. And it does the normal optimistic locking that Commit does, assuming the
125: 	// pessimistic locking passes. After this method runs, the two datasets given in |commitDS and |workingSetDS| are both
126: 	// updated in the new root, or neither of them are.
127: 	CommitWithWorkingSet(ctx context.Context, commitDS, workingSetDS Dataset, val types.Value, workingSetSpec WorkingSetSpec, prevWsHash hash.Hash, opts CommitOptions) (Dataset, Dataset, error)
128: 
129: 	// Delete removes the Dataset named ds.ID() from the map at the root of
130: 	// the Database. If the Dataset is already not present in the map,
131: 	// returns success. If a workinset path is provided, the Delete will also verify that the working set doesn't
132: 	// have changes which will be lost by the Delete before deleting it as well. If an empty working set path is
133: 	// provided, then no changes to the working set will be made.
134: 	//
135: 	// If the update cannot be performed, e.g., because of a conflict,
136: 	// Delete returns an 'ErrMergeNeeded' error.
137: 	Delete(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, workingSetPath string) (Dataset, error)
138: 
139: 	// SetHead ignores any lineage constraints (e.g. the current head being
140: 	// an ancestor of the new Commit) and force-sets a mapping from
141: 	// datasetID: addr in this database. addr can point to a Commit or a
142: 	// Tag, but if Dataset is already present in the Database, it must
143: 	// point to the type of struct.
144: 	//
145: 	// All values that have been written to this Database are guaranteed to
146: 	// be persistent after SetHead(). If the update cannot be performed,
147: 	// error will be non-nil.
148: 	// The workingSetPath is the path to the working set that should be used for updating the working set. If one
149: 	// is not provided, no working set update will be performed.
150: 	SetHead(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, newHeadAddr hash.Hash, workingSetPath string) (Dataset, error)
151: 
152: 	// FastForward sets the head of |ds| to the commit at |newHeadAddr| if it is a descendant of
153: 	// the current head. If the update cannot be performed, for example because another writer has
154: 	// moved the head concurrently, err will be non-nil.
155: 	// If |workingSetPath| is non-empty, the working set at that path is updated to match the new head.
156: 	// When |allowDirtyWorking| is true, the working set may have unstaged changes, such as ignored tables.
157: 	FastForward(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, newHeadAddr hash.Hash, workingSetPath string, allowDirtyWorking bool) (Dataset, error)
158: 
159: 	// Stats may return some kind of struct that reports statistics about the
160: 	// ChunkStore that backs this Database instance. The type is
161: 	// implementation-dependent, and impls may return nil
162: 	Stats() interface{}
163: 
164: 	// StatsSummary may return a string containing summarized statistics for
165: 	// the ChunkStore that backs this Database. It must return "Unsupported"
166: 	// if this operation is not supported.
167: 	StatsSummary() string
168: 
169: 	Format() *types.NomsBinFormat
170: 
171: 	// PersistGhostCommitIDs persists the given set of ghost commit IDs to the storage layer of the database. Ghost
172: 	// commits are commits which are real but have not been replicated to this instance of the database. Currently,
173: 	// it is only appropriate to use this method during a shallow clone operation.
174: 	PersistGhostCommitIDs(ctx context.Context, ghosts hash.HashSet) error
175: 
176: 	// chunkStore returns the ChunkStore used to read and write
177: 	// groups of values to the database efficiently. This interface is a low-
178: 	// level detail of the database that should infrequently be needed by
179: 	// clients.
180: 	chunkStore() chunks.ChunkStore
181: }

196:

200: }

202: // CanUsePuller returns true if a datas.Puller can be used to pull data from one Database into another.  Not all
203: // Databases support this yet.
204: func CanUsePuller(ctx context.Context, db Database) (bool, error) {
205: 	cs := db.chunkStore()
206: 	if tfs, ok := cs.(chunks.TableFileStore); ok {
207: 		ops, err := tfs.SupportedOperations(ctx)
208: 		if err != nil {
209: 			return false, err
210: 		}
211: 		return ops.CanRead && ops.CanWrite, nil
212: 	}
213: 	return false, nil
214: }
